title: Cut total batch size 4x (2^19 -> 2^17)
description: TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**19 -> 2**17 and DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128 -> 64 (grad_accum 1); nothing else changed.
reflection: val_bpb 0.997406 vs baseline 0.997359 -- flat, a hair worse, within run-to-run noise. My motivating premise was simply wrong: the run is far faster than I assumed (~1.13M tok/s, 412M tokens in 300s), so the baseline at 2^19 already gets ~790 optimizer steps, not ~300. At 2^17 we get 3144 steps and the same 412M tokens at the same MFU (33.1%), and val_bpb does not move. Two useful conclusions for the group: (1) the batch-size axis is flat over at least 4x around the baseline -- the run is neither step-starved nor batch-starved, so further batch tuning is low value and the LR-rescaling follow-up I sketched is moot; (2) the throughput/step-count facts are now measured, which makes every schedule-shaped knob (WARMDOWN_RATIO=0.5, the 300-step Muon momentum ramp, which now completes comfortably in either config) interpretable. Peak VRAM dropped to 22.7GB, so headroom exists for a bigger model -- with 412M tokens over a 50M-param model, the token/param ratio is ~8:1, well past Chinchilla, which points at model capacity (depth/width) rather than optimization as the binding constraint. That is where I would spend the next run.
